mainTopic: Admitting a signature on a שטר: רבי מאיר's ruling, רב הונא's rule on קיום, and who is not believed to claim a שטר אמנה
overview: The amud opens by explaining why, according to רבי מאיר, witnesses who confirm their signatures cannot cancel the שטר by saying 'we were minors' or 'we were forced.' The minors claim fails because of a חזקה that witnesses only sign for adults. For the forced claim, רב חסדא says one must die rather than sign a lie. רבא rejects this, because פיקוח נפש overrides everything except the three cardinal sins. So the גמרא explains רבי מאיר through רב הונא's rule: once someone admits he wrote a שטר, it needs no קיום. רב נחמן says this simply follows רבי מאיר, and he still makes lenders do קיום. Next, רב rules that someone who says 'this is a שטר אמנה' is not believed. The גמרא asks who the speaker is, and every option seems obvious or wrong. Then three answers follow: רבא says it is the borrower (through רב הונא), אביי says it is a lender who owes others (through רבי נתן), and רב אשי says it is the witnesses (through רב כהנא's ban on keeping a שטר אמנה).

steps.title: A presumption explains the minors claim
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why witnesses are not believed to say 'we were minors.' There is a חזקה that witnesses only sign a שטר made when the signers were adults.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a presumption that witnesses only sign a document if it was done when they were adults.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why, according to רבי מאיר, witnesses cannot cancel their signed שטר by claiming they were minors. Witnesses are assumed to sign only when everything was done properly by adults.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חזקה is a strong default assumption that a court relies on. Because of it, the claim 'we were minors' goes against what we assume about every signed שטר. So it is not accepted. This part of רבי מאיר's ruling is easy to explain, and it sets up the harder question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A legal presumption; what we assume is true by default
A legal document, such as a loan document
An adult, as opposed to a minor

phrases.english: There is a presumption that witnesses do not sign
on the document unless
it was done by an adult.

steps.triggerLanguage: חזקה אין העדים חותמין על השטר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes explaining the 'minors' part of רבי מאיר's view, which began before this text.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses are presumed to sign only on a שטר done by adults, so the claim 'we were minors' is not believed.

steps.title: What is the reason for the forced-signing claim?
steps.stepSummary: The minors claim makes sense, but why does רבי מאיר reject witnesses who say they were forced to sign?
steps.simpleTranslation: But when they say they were forced, what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי מאיר does not believe witnesses who say they were forced to sign. This question sets up the next few steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חזקה about adults does not help here. Being forced has nothing to do with age. So the גמרא needs a different reason why the claim 'we were forced' is rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: People who were forced or threatened
What is the reason?

phrases.english: But forced ones, what is the reason?
phrases.notes: He means the witnesses who say, 'Yes, that is our signature, but we were forced to sign.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the minors claim, which is explained, to the forced claim, which is not yet explained.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason רבי מאיר rejects the claim 'we were forced to sign.'

steps.title: רב חסדא: one must die rather than sign a lie
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says רבי מאיר holds that witnesses should let themselves be killed rather than sign falsely. So saying 'we were forced' means admitting a sin, and they are not believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: רבי מאיר holds that witnesses who were told 'Sign a lie or be killed' should be killed and not sign a lie.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question. According to רבי מאיר, signing falsely is forbidden even if your life is threatened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the witnesses were required to die rather than sign, then saying 'we were forced and signed anyway' means admitting they sinned. A person cannot make himself a רשע by his own testimony, so the claim is not accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds; this is his view
A lie or falsehood
They should be killed and not sign

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא, קָסָבַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: Rabbi Meir holds:
witnesses who were told
'Sign a lie and you will not be killed'
should be killed and not sign a lie.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב חסדא קסבר רבי מאיר
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר holds that one must die rather than sign falsely, so the forced claim is an admission of a sin and is not believed.

steps.title: רבא: saving a life overrides signing falsely
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects. If the witnesses had asked us beforehand, we would tell them to sign and live, because פיקוח נפש overrides everything except the three cardinal sins. So how can we blame them after they signed?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Now, if they had come to us for advice, we would tell them, 'Go sign and do not get killed.' The Master said that nothing stands in the way of saving a life except עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות and שפיכות דמים. Now that they signed, would we ask them, 'Why did you sign?'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב חסדא's answer. Signing falsely is not one of the three sins a person must die for, so the witnesses did nothing wrong by signing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of פיקוח נפש says almost every איסור gives way to save a life. The only exceptions are עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות and שפיכות דמים. Since signing falsely is not one of those three, the witnesses were allowed to sign. Their claim is not an admission of a sin, so רב חסדא's reason falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: To consult; to ask for advice
Saving a life, which overrides almost all laws
Idol worship
Forbidden sexual relations
Murder

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the forced claim is believed. He agrees with the ruling. He is only rejecting רב חסדא's reason for it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This states the basic rule that only the three cardinal sins require giving up one's life. Everything else gives way to פיקוח נפש.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
Now, if they had come before us to ask for advice,
we would say to them:
'Go sign, and do not get killed,'
as the Master said:
There is nothing that stands
in the way of saving a life
except idol worship, forbidden relations,
and murder alone.
Now that they already signed, would we say to them:
'Why did you sign?'

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה רבא השתא אילו אתו לקמן לאמלוכי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב חסדא's answer from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that רבי מאיר requires dying rather than signing falsely.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: פיקוח נפש overrides everything except the three cardinal sins. Signing falsely is not one of them, so signing under threat is allowed and is not an admission of a sin.

steps.title: New reason: an admitted שטר needs no further proof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops רב חסדא's reason and explains רבי מאיר through רב הונא in the name of רב: once someone admits he wrote a שטר, it does not need קיום. The witnesses' admission of their signatures makes the שטר valid, and they cannot then undo it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי מאיר's reason follows what רב הונא said in the name of רב: if someone admits he wrote a document, it does not need to be confirmed in court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new explanation for רבי מאיר that does not depend on dying rather than signing. It uses רב הונא's rule about an admitted שטר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a שטר needs קיום, meaning a court confirms the signatures. If the person admits he wrote it, that admission is enough to confirm it. In the same way, once the witnesses say 'this is our signature,' the שטר is already confirmed. Their added claim 'we were forced' cannot take that away.

keyTerms.meaning: One who admits
To confirm it; to have the court verify the signatures (קיום שטרות)
There is no need

steps.whatToRemember: According to the final answer, רבי מאיר rejects 'we were forced' because the witnesses' own admission of their signatures already makes the שטר valid, just as רב הונא rules that an admitted שטר needs no קיום. It is not because signing under threat is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: רב הונא's rule, that an admitted שטר needs no קיום, is an important principle in the laws of documents and loans.

phrases.english: Rather, the reason of Rabbi Meir
is like what Rav Huna said in the name of Rav.
For Rav Huna said in the name of Rav:
One who admits about a document that he wrote it,
phrases.notes: This is talking about a borrower who says, 'Yes, I wrote this loan document.'

phrases.english: there is no need to confirm it in court.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא טעמא דרבי מאיר כדרב הונא אמר רב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts רבא's challenge and replaces רב חסדא's reason with a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the rejected reason with a different principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר rejects the forced claim because signing under threat is a sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר rejects it because admitting one's signature confirms the שטר, following רב הונא's rule that an admitted שטר needs no קיום.

steps.title: רב הונא's rule: an admitted document needs no ratification
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רב הונא's statement in the name of רב: if the borrower admits he wrote a שטר, the lender does not need קיום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the statement itself. רב הונא said in the name of רב: if someone admits he wrote a document, it does not need to be ratified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the rule it quoted in the last step and now looks at it on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a lender has to prove a שטר is real through קיום, by checking the witnesses' signatures. רב הונא says that if the borrower himself admits he wrote it, that admission is enough proof. Before this, the rule was only used to explain רבי מאיר. Now it is examined on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself: a return to a statement quoted earlier in order to discuss it directly
One who admits that a document is genuine
Ratifying a document in court by confirming the signatures

phrases.english: The matter itself.
phrases.notes: This takes us back to רב הונא's rule, which was just quoted in step 5.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said that Rav said:
One who admits about a document that he wrote it,
it does not need to be ratified.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא. אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the rule used as the answer in step 5 and looks at it directly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A borrower's admission that he wrote the שטר makes קיום unnecessary.

steps.title: רב נחמן: just say you follow רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן objects to how רב הונא worded his rule. He says it is really the view of רבי מאיר, so רב הונא should say that openly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: Why are you hiding it like a thief? If you agree with רבי מאיר, just say 'the הלכה follows רבי מאיר.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן challenges רב הונא for stating the rule as if it had no source, when it really comes from רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן is not attacking the logic of the rule. He is attacking the way it was presented. A rule stated plainly sounds like everyone agrees with it, but this one belongs to one side of a dispute between תנאים. רב נחמן wants רב הונא to admit he is choosing sides.

keyTerms.meaning: Sneaking something in like a thief: hiding where an opinion comes from
The law follows רבי מאיר
You hold, you are of the opinion

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to him:
Why do you need to sneak it in like a thief?
phrases.notes: He means you are hiding where your rule comes from, as if it were stolen goods.

phrases.english: If you hold like Rabbi Meir,
say: the halacha follows Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how the rule in step 6 is presented.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's presentation of the rule as if no one disputed it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule matches only רבי מאיר, so stating it plainly hides the fact that the תנאים argue about it.

steps.title: רב הונא asks רב נחמן for his own view
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא turns the question around and asks what רב נחמן himself holds.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: And what does the Master hold?
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא asks רב נחמן for his own position. This sets up רב נחמן's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב נחמן does not follow רבי מאיר, he must handle an admitted שטר some other way. רב הונא wants to hear what that way is.

keyTerms.meaning: Master: a respectful way of saying 'you'
How

phrases.english: He said to him:
And how does the Master hold?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רב נחמן's criticism by asking for his own position.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רב נחמן's own ruling on a שטר that the borrower admits to writing

steps.title: רב נחמן: lenders must still ratify their documents
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says that when lenders come to his court, he tells them to do קיום on their documents first and then come for judgment.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: When they come before us for judgment, we tell them: 'Go ratify your documents, and then come down for judgment.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers that he does not follow רב הונא's rule. He still requires קיום even when the borrower admits the שטר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the lender relies only on the borrower's admission, the borrower can add 'yes I wrote it, but I already paid.' Once the שטר is confirmed through the witnesses, that claim no longer works. So רב נחמן wants the שטר confirmed independently.

keyTerms.meaning: Go
Come down to judgment: stand before the court
Before us

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא follows רבי מאיר: an admitted שטר needs no קיום. רב נחמן disagrees and still makes lenders do קיום.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כִּי אָתוּ לְקַמַּן לְדִינָא,
phrases.english: He said to him: When they come before us for judgment,
we say to them:
"Go ratify your documents
and come down for judgment."

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אָתוּ לְקַמַּן לְדִינָא אָמְרִינַן לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב הונא's question from step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב נחמן requires קיום even when the borrower admits the שטר.

steps.title: רב's rule about a document of trust
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: someone who says 'this is a שטר אמנה' is not believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: someone who says 'this is a document of trust' is not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule. It is about someone who claims a שטר was written in trust and no loan ever happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שטר אמנה is a loan document written ahead of time, before the money was actually given. Someone claiming this is saying the שטר looks real but no debt exists. רב says such a person is not believed, but he does not say who the person is.

keyTerms.meaning: A document of trust: written ahead of a loan that never actually happened
He is not believed
One who says

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
One who says "This is a document of trust"
phrases.notes: He means the שטר was written in trust beforehand, but no money was ever actually lent.

phrases.english: is not believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב הָאוֹמֵר שְׁטַר אֲמָנָה הוּא זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new but related topic: claims that weaken a שטר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A claim that a שטר is a שטר אמנה is not believed.

steps.title: Who is making the claim?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who it is that says the שטר is a שטר אמנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the one saying it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who רב is talking about. This sets up a list of possibilities in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer changes everything. A borrower, a lender, or a witness saying this would each be judged very differently.

keyTerms.meaning: Who
That is saying

phrases.english: Who is the one saying it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks who is meant in רב's rule from step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which person's claim of שטר אמנה רב is talking about

steps.title: Not the borrower: that would be obvious
steps.stepSummary: If the borrower says it, of course he is not believed, so רב would not need to teach it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the borrower is saying it, that is obvious. Is it up to him?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the borrower as the speaker and rejects it, because the rule would be too obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A borrower cannot cancel a valid שטר against himself just by saying so. Everyone already knows that, so רב must mean someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say: introduces a possibility the גמרא is testing
Borrower
It is obvious
Is it in his power? He has no power to do this

phrases.english: If you say that the borrower is saying it,
it is obvious; is it up to him?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rules out the borrower as the speaker in רב's rule
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rule would teach something obvious

steps.title: Not the lender: he deserves a blessing
steps.stepSummary: If the lender says it, he is giving up his own claim, so of course he is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say the lender is saying it. Let a blessing come upon him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the lender as the speaker and rejects it, because he would surely be believed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lender who says his own שטר is not a real debt is admitting against himself. He is not only believed, he deserves praise for his honesty. So רב cannot mean him either.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather: moves to another possibility
Lender
May a blessing come upon him

phrases.english: But rather, if the lender is saying it,
let a blessing come upon him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא דְּקָאָמַר מַלְוֶה תָּבוֹא עָלָיו בְּרָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the second possible answer after the borrower was ruled out in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rules out the lender as the speaker in רב's rule
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A lender admitting against himself would surely be believed

steps.title: The witnesses? Either obvious or puzzling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the witnesses are the ones saying it. If their signatures are known from elsewhere, it is obvious they are not believed. If not, why shouldn't they be believed?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the witnesses are saying it. If their handwriting can be confirmed from somewhere else, it is obvious they are not believed. And if their handwriting cannot be confirmed from somewhere else, why are they not believed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the witnesses as the speakers and finds a problem with both possible versions of that case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the signatures can be checked from other documents, the שטר stands without the witnesses, so their later claim does not count. That is too obvious to need רב's teaching. If the שטר is confirmed only through their own word, then the same mouth that made it valid can also limit it (הפה שאסר הוא הפה שהתיר). So רב's rule seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses
Their handwriting, their signatures
Comes out from another place: can be confirmed from other documents
They are believed
Why

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new rule about witnesses. The גמרא is stuck because every choice of speaker seems to make רב's rule either obvious or wrong.

phrases.english: Rather, the witnesses are saying it.

phrases.aramaic: אִי דִּכְתַב יָדָם יוֹצֵא מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר —
phrases.english: If their handwriting comes out from another place,
phrases.notes: Their signatures can be matched against other documents, so the court does not need them to confirm it.

phrases.english: it is obvious that they are not believed.
And if their handwriting does not
come out from another place,
why are they not believed?
phrases.notes: The שטר is valid only because they say so, so why not believe the rest of what they say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries the last remaining speaker after the borrower and lender were ruled out, and runs into a dilemma.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that a claim of שטר אמנה is not believed, applied to witnesses
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the signatures can be confirmed elsewhere, the rule is obvious. If they cannot, the witnesses should be believed because the same mouth that made the שטר valid can limit it. Either way, רב's rule seems unnecessary or wrong.

steps.title: רבא: It Is the Borrower, Following רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the one claiming אמנה is the borrower. The new point comes from רב הונא's rule: once a borrower admits he wrote a document, it needs no further verification.
steps.simpleTranslation: (A memory sign: בא״ש.) רבא said: really it is the borrower who says it, and it follows רב הונא. רב הונא said in the name of רב: someone who admits that he wrote a document does not need to have it verified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first gives a memory sign for the three answers that are coming. Then רבא answers that רב was talking about the borrower after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא said it was obvious that a borrower is not believed. רבא explains the case: the borrower admits he wrote the document, so by רב הונא's rule the lender does not need to verify it in court. רב is teaching that once the borrower makes that admission, he cannot cancel the document by adding 'but it was only a שטר אמנה'.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory sign that helps you remember the order of the opinions
'Really' or 'actually'. It signals a return to an option that was rejected earlier
Borrower
One who admits that he wrote the document
To verify the document in court by confirming the witnesses' signatures

phrases.english: (A memory sign: B-A-Sh)
phrases.notes: The letters stand for רבא, אביי and רב אשי, the three answers coming up in order.

phrases.english: Rava said: Actually, it is the borrower who says it,
and it follows Rav Huna.
For Rav Huna said in the name of Rav:
One who admits about a document that he wrote it
does not need to have it verified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem in step 14 by going back to the borrower option that step 12 rejected.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case more narrowly: the borrower first admitted he wrote the document
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A borrower saying 'אמנה' is obviously not believed, so רב would have nothing new to teach.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is one where the borrower admits writing the document. That makes it valid without verification, and his אמנה claim cannot undo it.

steps.title: אביי: It Is the Lender Who Owes Money to Others
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the one claiming אמנה is the lender. The case is one where the lender himself owes money to other people, following רבי נתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: really it is the lender who says it, and the case is where he owes money to others, and it follows רבי נתן.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second answer. He goes back to the lender option and limits it to a lender who has his own creditors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא said a lender is believed because he is only giving up his own money. אביי points out that if the lender owes money to others, his admission would hurt them. Under רבי נתן's rule, the lender's creditors could collect straight from the borrower, so the lender cannot wipe out the debt with his words.

keyTerms.meaning: Lender
Causes a loss to others, or owes to others

phrases.english: Abaye said: Actually, it is the lender who says it,
and the case is where he owes money to others,
phrases.notes: He means the lender has his own debts, so throwing away this document would hurt his creditors.

phrases.english: and it follows Rabbi Natan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from רבא's by going back to the lender option that step 13 rejected.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case more narrowly: the lender has creditors of his own
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A lender who says 'אמנה' is only giving up his own claim, so of course he is believed.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the lender owes others, his admission harms his creditors, so he is not believed.

steps.title: רבי נתן's Rule: Collecting From Your Debtor's Debtor
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא of רבי נתן: if A is owed by B, and B is owed by C, A may collect directly from C. This is learned from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא, רבי נתן says: how do we know that if one person is owed a מנה by his friend, and that friend is owed by another, we take from the last one and give to the first? The פסוק says: 'And he shall give to the one he is guilty to.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source of רבי נתן's rule, which אביי relied on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן teaches that a debt can be collected straight from the debtor's own debtor. That is why the lender's creditor has a real claim on the borrower's money. So when the lender says 'this was only a שטר אמנה,' he is taking something away from his own creditor.

keyTerms.meaning: A creditor, someone who is owed money
A sum of one hundred זוז
'The verse teaches'. It introduces a source from a פסוק
We take from this one and give to that one: collecting directly from the debtor's debtor

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Natan says:
From where do we know, for one who is owed a maneh by his friend,
and that friend is owed by another friend,
from where do we know that we take from this one and give to that one?
phrases.notes: בית דין takes from the last debtor and pays the first creditor directly, skipping the person in the middle.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"And he shall give to the one to whom he is guilty."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the רבי נתן rule that אביי's answer depends on.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that the lender's creditors are hurt by his admission
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי נתן based on במדבר 5:7

steps.title: רב אשי: It Is the Witnesses, Following רב כהנא
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the ones claiming אמנה are the witnesses, and their handwriting is not known from anywhere else. They are still not believed, because of רב כהנא's teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: really it is the witnesses who say it, and their handwriting is not known from elsewhere. As for your question, 'Why should they not be believed?', it follows רב כהנא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a third answer. He takes the witness option and answers the exact question from step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14 the גמרא asked: if the witnesses' handwriting cannot be confirmed any other way, why aren't they believed? The only proof of the signatures comes from the witnesses themselves. רב אשי says the reason comes from רב כהנא, whose statement follows next. It teaches that a שטר אמנה is something forbidden, so the witnesses would be admitting they took part in something wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses
Their handwriting, meaning their signatures
Known or confirmed from somewhere else
They are believed

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם דְּקָאָמְרִי עֵדִים.
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Actually, it is the witnesses who say it.

phrases.aramaic: וּדְאֵין כְּתַב יָדָם יוֹצֵא מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר.
phrases.english: And it is where their handwriting is not known from another place.
And as for what you said, 'Why are they not believed?'
It is like Rav Kahana.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם דְּקָאָמְרִי עֵדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer, which keeps the witness option from step 14 and responds to its question directly.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Answering the question directly by bringing a supporting rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: When the witnesses' signatures can only be confirmed through them, they should be believed when they say it was a שטר אמנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are not believed because, according to רב כהנא, a שטר אמנה is forbidden.

steps.title: רב כהנא: It Is Forbidden to Keep a שטר אמנה
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא teaches that it is forbidden to keep a שטר אמנה in one's house, based on the פסוק 'Let not injustice dwell in your tents.'
steps.simpleTranslation: For רב כהנא said: it is forbidden for a person to leave a שטר אמנה in his house, as it says: 'Let not injustice dwell in your tents.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רב כהנא's statement, which רב אשי relied on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שטר אמנה is a document that could later be used to collect a debt that never existed, so keeping one is forbidden. That is why witnesses who say 'we signed a שטר אמנה' are not believed. They would be saying they took part in something forbidden. This completes the three answers to רב's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Leave it lying around, keep it
A loan document written 'on trust' before any money was lent
Injustice, wrongdoing

steps.whatToRemember: There are three ways to explain רב's 'not believed': the borrower who already admitted writing the document (רבא, through רב הונא), the lender who owes others (אביי, through רבי נתן), and the witnesses (רב אשי, through רב כהנא's ban on keeping a שטר אמנה).
steps.whyThisMatters: רב כהנא's rule turns a שטר אמנה from a harmless arrangement into something forbidden. That changes how we judge anyone who claims one was written.

phrases.english: For Rav Kahana said:
It is forbidden for a person to keep
a document of trust inside his house,
because it is said:
"Let not injustice dwell in your tents."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the רב כהנא rule that רב אשי's answer depends on.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's claim that the witnesses are not believed
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב כהנא's ruling, based on איוב 11:14
